prompt.adult: In Luke 15:8, a woman has ten silver coins and loses one. What is the first thing she does?
prompt.child: Jesus told about a woman who lost one of her ten coins. What did she do first to look for it?
prompt.teen: Luke 15:8: what does she do before she will “sweep the house”?
prompt.older: According to Luke 15:8, what does the woman do first after losing one coin?

verses.text: “Or what woman, having ten silver coins, if she loses one coin, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?

explanation.adult: Read the middle of 15:8, after “does not.”
explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 8.
explanation.teen: 15:8 lists three things she does. Read the first.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:8 goes on: she sweeps the house and searches carefully until she finds it. 15:9 says she calls others to rejoice with her.
teaching.takeaway: She would light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully.

prompt.adult: The rich man in Luke 12 had no room to store his crops. In 12:18, after pulling down his barns, what does he plan to do?
prompt.child: A rich farmer had too many crops for his barns. What did he plan to do after tearing them down?
prompt.teen: Luke 12:18: “I will pull down my barns and” do what?
prompt.older: According to Luke 12:18, what will the rich man do after pulling down his barns?

verses.text: So he said, ‘I will do this: I will pull down my barns and build greater, and there I will store all my crops and my goods.

explanation.adult: Read the middle of 12:18, after “pull down my barns and.”
explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 18.
explanation.teen: 12:18 has two plans: pull down, then a second. Read the second.
explanation.older: It follows “pull down my barns and” in 12:18.

teaching.extended_explanation: 12:17 says he thought within himself, “What shall I do, since I have no room to store my crops?” 12:19 goes on to what he will say to his soul.
teaching.takeaway: He said, “I will pull down my barns and build greater.”

prompt.adult: In the parable of the great supper, guests began to make excuses. In 14:19, what did the second say he had bought?
prompt.child: Guests invited to a big dinner made excuses. One said he had bought some animals. What did he buy?
prompt.older: According to Luke 14:19, what had the second guest bought?

verses.text: But they all with one accord began to make excuses. The first said to him, ‘I have bought a piece of ground, and I must go and see it. I ask you to have me excused.’
And another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them. I ask you to have me excused.’

explanation.adult: Read the start of 14:19, after “I have bought.”
explanation.child: Look near the start of verse 19.
explanation.teen: 14:18 has the first excuse; 14:19 has the second. Read what he bought.

teaching.extended_explanation: 14:18 says the first had bought a piece of ground and must go and see it. 14:19 ends, “I ask you to have me excused.”
teaching.takeaway: He said, “I have bought five yoke of oxen.”

prompt.adult: The unjust steward asks the first debtor how much he owes: a hundred measures of oil. In 16:6, what number does the steward tell him to write?
prompt.child: A dishonest manager asked a man who owed a hundred measures of oil to change his bill. What number did he tell him to write?
prompt.teen: Luke 16:6: “Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write” what?
prompt.older: According to Luke 16:6, what did the steward tell the first debtor to write?

verses.text: “So he called every one of his master’s debtors to him, and said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
And he said, ‘A hundred measures of oil.’ So he said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’

explanation.child: Look at the end of verse 6.
explanation.teen: 16:6 gives the debt first and then the steward’s order. Read what he says to write.
explanation.older: It follows “sit down quickly and write” in 16:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:5 says he called each of the debtors to him. 16:7 tells of a second debtor who owed wheat.
teaching.takeaway: He told him to sit down quickly and write fifty.

prompt.adult: Two men went up to the temple to pray. In 18:13, standing afar off, what did the second man do as he asked God for mercy?
prompt.child: In Jesus’ story, one man at the temple would not even look up. What did he do while he prayed for mercy?
prompt.teen: Luke 18:13: he “would not so much as raise his eyes to heaven, but” did what?
prompt.older: According to Luke 18:13, what did the man standing afar off do as he prayed?

verses.text: “Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
And the tax collector, standing afar off, would not so much as raise his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me a sinner!’

explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 13.
explanation.teen: 18:13 says where he stood, where he would not look, and then what he did. Read the third part.

teaching.extended_explanation: 18:10 says one was a Pharisee. 18:13 ends with his prayer: “God, be merciful to me a sinner!”
teaching.takeaway: He “beat his breast,” praying for mercy.

prompt.adult: Luke 12:21 warns about one who is not rich toward God. In 16:13, you cannot serve God and what?
prompt.child: Jesus said no one can serve two masters. You cannot serve God and what else?
prompt.teen: Luke 16:13: “You cannot serve God and” what?
prompt.older: Linking Luke 12:21 with 16:13, what cannot be served along with God?

verses.text: “So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
“No servant can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be loyal to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.”

explanation.child: Look at the very end of verse 13.
explanation.teen: 12:21 is the setting; 16:13 closes with a short statement. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 12:21 speaks of one who lays up treasure for himself. 16:13 opens, “No servant can serve two masters.”

prompt.adult: In 14:21 the master sends for the poor, maimed, lame, and blind. In 15:9, when the woman finds her coin, whom does she call together?
prompt.child: When the woman found her lost coin, she wanted others to celebrate with her. Whom did she call?
prompt.older: Alongside the invitation of 14:21, whom does the woman call together in 15:9?

verses.text: So that servant came and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor and the maimed and the lame and the blind.’
And when she has found it, she calls her friends and neighbors together, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the piece which I lost!’

explanation.adult: Read the start of 15:9, after “she calls.”
explanation.child: Look near the start of verse 9.
explanation.teen: 14:21 is the setting; 15:9 names who is called and then what she says. Read who.

teaching.extended_explanation: 14:21 sends the servant into the streets and lanes of the city. 15:9 has her say, “Rejoice with me, for I have found the piece which I lost!”
teaching.takeaway: She calls her friends and neighbors together.

prompt.adult: Luke 12:16 begins a parable about a rich man’s ground. In 16:2, what does another rich man tell the manager of his goods to give?
prompt.child: A rich man heard his manager was wasting his goods. What did he tell the manager to give him?
prompt.older: Alongside the rich man of 12:16, what does the master in 16:2 demand of the man who managed his goods?

choices.text: the money you have kept for yourself
a list of all the debtors

verses.text: Then He spoke a parable to them, saying: “The ground of a certain rich man yielded plentifully.
So he called him and said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.’

explanation.child: Look in the second half of verse 16:2.
explanation.teen: 12:16 is the setting; 16:2 asks a question and then gives an order. Read the order.

teaching.extended_explanation: 12:16 says the ground yielded plentifully. 16:2 begins with the master asking, “What is this I hear about you?”
teaching.takeaway: He said, “Give an account of your stewardship.”
